*241. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) the number of new telephone exchanges installed in Uttar Pradesh, Orissa, 
Rajasthan, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and NER during the last three years, district-
wise and year-wise;

Statement

Modernisation of employment exchanges 
*242 SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN: W ill the Minister of LABOUR be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government have taken any steps to modernise the 
employment exchanges and to collect accurate and reliable statistics on the rate 
of unemployment; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (SHRI SAHIB SINGH VERMA): (a) and 
(b) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
4 

[5 December, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
Statement 
The employment exchanges are under the administrative and financial control 
of the respective States/UT Governments and these are being modernized 
according to their financial capacity. At  present 363 out of 939 employment 
exchanges are computerized. 
Reliable estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained from the 
quinquennial labour force surveys conducted by the National Sample Survey 
Organisation. Job-seekers registered with the employment exchanges are not 
necessarily unemployed and it is also not necessary that all the unemployed 
should register with the employment exchanges. Therefore, the employment 
exchange data provides details of the job seekers registered and not the 
complete picture of unemployment in the country. 
SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN: Sir, my question focuses on the statistical data 
about unemployment which is primarily obtained from the employment exchanges 
in the organised sector. Of course, in the unorganised sector, only sample surveys 
are done. So, the quality of data is hardly useful. As you know, Sir, in the 
Western countries the rate of unemploym ent is a very crucial parameter for 
the evaluation of the economy. We have no such reliable data about the exact 
number of unemployed people. The employment exchanges work at more than 
900 places and they collect data only from establishments which are employing 
more than 25 people in the organised sector. There is the Compulsory Notification 
of Vacancies Act. But the employment exchanges are monitored by the State 
Governments. What is the punitive action taken against the companies which 
do not notify vacancies? Our experience is that nobody bothers to inform the 
employment exchanges about the exis ting vacancies. They advertise the 
vacancies in the newspapers. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: You have already put your question. Let him answer. 
SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN: I would like to know whether the 
Compulsory Notification of Vacancies Act is being followed or not.

Supply of rice to BPL families 
*244. SHRI A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the news report captioned "Right 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2002] 
to food still a dream" which appeared in The Hindu' dated the 24th October, 2002; 
(b) if so, what steps would be taken to provide rice to families Living Below 
the Poverty Line as directed by the Supreme Court; 
(c) what action Government propose to take so that price of the rice through 
ration shop is fixed as per the purchasing capacity of these families living in 
extreme poverty; 
(d) whether any action plan is proposed to be formulated to help villagers 
in various parts of the country who are bracing themselves for extreme hunger 
in months ahead due to crop failure; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND- PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on 
the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) to (e) The Central Government have been making allocations of 
foodgrains under the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) to the State 
Governments and UT Administrations for distribution amongst the BPL 
families @ 35 kg per family per month. The Central Issue Prices for the BPL 
families are highly subsidized and have remained unchanged since July, 2000. 
In order to address the needs of one crore poorest of the poor families, the 
Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) is being implemented in all parts of the country 
under which foodgrains are issued @ Rs. 2 a kg for wheat and Rs. 3 a kg for 
rice at the retail level.Under the Special Component of the Sampoorna Gramin 
Rojgar Yojana (SGRY), the foodgrains are provided, free of cost, to the States 
affected by natural calamities such as flood, cyclone and drought for 
generation of additional employment oppo rtunities, alongwith food security, 
through creation of durable community assets in the rural areas. So, far, about 
38.29 lakh MTs of foodgrains have been allotted to 16 drought/natural calamity 
affected States under the Special Component of the SGRY during the current 
financial year.

†260. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN': 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Planning Commission has taken a decision to ascertain the 
number of people living Below Poverty Line in each State; 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
37 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2002] 
(b) if so, whether Government had also finalized any policy to ascertain such 
numbers; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the difference between the old and new 
procedure and policy? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) and (b) The Planning Commission 
has been estimating the incidence of pov erty at National and State level since 
the late 1970s. The estimates of poverty were initially made from the method 
outlined in the Task Force on Projection of Minimum Needs and Effective 
Consumption Demand. Th is method was replaced by the methodology 
contained in the Report of the Expert Group on Estimation of Proportion and 
Number of Poor {commonly known as Lakdawala Committee, named after its 
Chairman) in March 1997 to estimate the poverty ratio (also known as the 
Head-Count ratio) at National and State level. According to this method, the 
percentage of people below the poverty line is estimated from state-specific 
poverty lines and state-specific consumer expenditure distribution, obtained from 
the large sample surveys on household consumer expenditure conducted by the 
NSSO once in approximately five years. Using this method, the poverty 
estimates of all the previous years have been re-worked and are available for 
the years 1973-74, 1977-78,1983,1987-88, 1993-94 and 1999-2000. 
(c) The Planning Commission in 1977 constituted a Task Force on 
Minimum Needs and Effective Consumption Demands which defined the 
poverty line as per capita expenditure level at which the average per capita per 
day calorie in take was 2400 kcal in rural areas and 2100 kcal in urban areas.The 
monetary equivalent of these norms were calculated as monthly per capita 
consumption expenditure of Rs.49.09 in rural areas and Rs. 56.64 in urban areas 
for 1973-74.These poverty lines were applied uniformly to all the States. Second, 
in order to ensure consistency with the national aggregates, the NSS consumer 
expenditure data was adjusted to the level of CSO consumption on a pro-rata basis 
across all expenditure classes. Using the poverty lines and the adjusted 
expenditure class-wise distribution of persons obtained from the national sample 
survey data on consumer expenditure of the States, the State-wise estimates of 
poverty were made. 
This methodology for estimation of poverty at National and State level 
was regarded by some as inappropriate and even inadequate in 
38 

[5 December. 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
giving a representative picture of incidence of poverty in India. In September 
1989, Planning Commission constituted an Expert Group to look into the 
methodology for estimation of poverty and to redefine the poverty line, if 
necessary. The Expert Group submitted its Report in July, 1993. 
The Expert Group did no t redefine the poverty line and accepted the one 
defined by the Task Force which was at national level. However, it 
recommended the disaggregation of the national poverty line into state-wise 
poverty lines in order to reflect the State-wise price differential. The important 
points of departure between the Expert Group methodology and the Task 
Force methodology are: 
(a) tn the new method, the NSS consumption expenditure data are not 
adjusted in any way and it is used as It is. 
(b) The new method uses State-wise poverty lines as against national level 
poverty line used in the old method. 
(c) The new method uses State-specific cost of Irving indices for updating the 
poverty line separately in rural and urban areas.The old method used only one 
all-India Index which is also same for rural and urban areas. 
The full Planning Commission under the Chairmanship of Prime Minister 
accepted its recommendations with minor modifications in March, 1997.

Disposal of nuclear waste 
1658. SHRI PARMESHWAR KUMAR AGARWALLA: Will the PRIME 
MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) what is the present system of disposal of nuclear waste; and 
(b) whether the method followed by in the country is as per the 
international standards and the norms followed by the developed countries? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ATOMIC 
ENERGY (SHRIMATI VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) Radioactive wastes in 
different physical forms viz., solid, liquid and gaseous, are generated during 
operation and maintenance of nuclear reactors. The gaseous and liquid 
effluents are decontaminated by suitable treatment processes to ensure that the 
radioactive contents of the treated ef fluent are well within the permissible 
specified limits for discharge into the environment and the radioactivity is 
concentrated in small volumes. The concentrate from the liquid and solid 
wastes are immobilised in solid materials like cement, bitumen, polymers etc 
so that the radioactivity will not leach out and re-enter the bio-sphere. This 
conditioned' waste is packaged in suitable containers and placed in reinforced 
concrete trenches, tile 
47

holes and vaults, located in access controlled areas, which are under constant 
surveillance. 
(b) The method followed by India for disposal of nuclear waste is as per 
international standards and as followed by developed countries. The disposal 
operations are carried out under the surveillance of regulatory authorities.

1673. SHRI JANARDHANA POOJ ARY : Will the Minister of

state : 
(a) whether It is a fact that there is possibility to increase teledensity 
through WLL technology at comparatively lesser cost than the fixed 
telephone lines; 
69 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2002] 
(b) if so, the details thereof with elucidation in comparative terms the salient 
features of the fixed line telephone and WLL-technology based telephone; 
(c) the steps taken by Government to increase the tele-density adopting 
WLL technology within the next two financial year; 
 
(d) whether Government are considering to achieve the target through 
reduced rent and tariff on WLL based telephones; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. 
SANJAY PASWAN) : (a) and (b) WLL (Wireless in Local Loop) is playing an 
Important role in deployment of telephones in the country. However, it is not 
possible to establish a definite correlation between tele-density and the cost of 
provision of WLL as tele-density depends upon provision of telephones which 
in turn depends upon demands for telephones. The salient features of fixed 
lines telephones and WLL technology based telephones are : 
In fixed line telephones, connections are provided through a pair of 
normally copper cable to each subs criber, whereas in WLL system 
connections are provided on wireless technology Laying of underground cable is 
time consuming, whereas WLL deployment is fast. Interruption in service will 
be there whenever cable is cut in fixed line connections due to man 
made/natural calamities, whereas interruption in WLL are not dependent on 
such eventualities except equipment fault. Fixed line telephone on copper cable 
are able to provide higher data rates compared to the presently deployed WLL 
systems though in future deployments this difference will disappear. 
(c) The Government through its Public sector units i.e. Bharat Sanchar 
Nigam Limited (BSNL) & Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited (MTNL) 
are planning to deploy 29^7 lakh lines on WLL during the next two 
financial years. 
(d) and (e) Tariff is fixed by Telecom Regulatory Authority of India 
(TRAI) who have absolute powers to fix it and Government has no rote 
in tariff fixation.

Statement 
Steps taken by the Government to Dispose of the Excess 
Stock of Foodgrains 
(i) The scale of'issue for APL, BPL and Antyodaya households has been 
Increased to 35 from 25 kg. per household per month. 
(ii) The scale of issue for all welfare institutions are hostels has been fixed 
uniformly @ 15 kg. per head per month. An additional allocation equal to 5% of 
the BPL allocation of States/UTs on this  account has been made for the year 
2002-2003 at BPL, GIR

provide WTO compatible subsidies for exports of wheat, wheat products and 
rice.

wheat products, subject to the condition that the stocks in the Central Pool 
will not be lower than the buffer stock of 243 lakh MTs (100 lakh MTs of 
rice and 143 lakh MTs of wheat) at any point of time.

countries on terms to be decided on a case-to-case basis.

1696. SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:

(b) the steps taken to ensure clearance of dues by the sugar mills in a time 
bound programme to avert unhappy situation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI V. SREENIVASA 
PRASAD): (a) A statement showing State-wise position of sugarcane price 
payable, price paid and the balance outstanding for the season 2001 -2002, as 
on 30.9.2002 is annexed. {See below) 
(b) The responsibility for ensuring timely payment of cane price dues lies 
with the State Governments which have necessary powers and field 
organizations to enforce such payments. The Central Government on its part, 
besides writing to the State Governments from time to time for expeditious 
clearance of the same, has taken the fo llowing remedial measures to improve 
the financial health of domestic sugar industry with a view to enabling it to 
reduce the cane price arrears: 
(i) The levy obligation of domestic sugar factories was reduced from 40% 
to 30% with effect from 01.01.2000 and, subsequently, to 15% with 
effect from 01.02.2001; this has further been reduced to 10% with effect 
from 01.03.2002 and will enable the sugar factories to sell more 
sugar under free sale quota In the open market and obtain better 
realization. 
(ii) To restrict the inflow of imported sugar in the country, the Central 
Government (with effect from 09.02.2000) has increased the 
customs duty to 60% along with the existing countervailing duty of 
Rs. 850 per tonne. 
103 

RAJYA SABHA [5 December, 2002] 
(iii) The Central Government is pursuing a policy of encouraging stability and 
reasonable level of sugar prices in the domestic market through judicious 
releases of free sale sugar quotas to enable the sugar factories to clear 
the cane price dues of the farmers. 
(iv) In order to liquidate the stocks of the sugar mills, the Government has 
allowed export of sugar. The quantitative ceiling on export of sugar as 
well as the requirement of registration with Agricultural and 
Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 
have been dispensed with, with effect from 01.04.2001. 
(v) In order to encourage the export of sugar, the Sugar Development Fund 
(SDF) Act, 1982 and the SDF Rules, 1983 have been amended, 
enabling reimbursement of the inte rnal transport & freight charges 
on export shipments of sugar. 
(vi) The Government has decided to create a buffer stock of 20 lakh tonnes 
of sugar for a period of one year. This will enable the sugar mills to 
get a subsidy amount of Rs. 412 crore from the Sugar Development 
Fund. In addition, an amount of Rs. 374 crores would be available 
from the banks to the mills on account  of buffer stock. Thus, a total 
amount of Rs. 786 crores would be provided to the mills enabling 
them to clear the payment of cane price dues to the sugarcane growers. 
This will also help the sugar industry to mitigate the financial 
hardship.

Threat posed to Dolphins in Chilka Lake 
MISS MABEL REBELLO (Madhya Pradesh): Madam, tourist boats in 
Chilka lake of Orissa are causing a se rious threat to the life of dolphins. 
According to the Wildlife Society of Orissa, 11 dolphins were killed during the 
last two years. Two dolphins were killed last month. Recognised as an 
endangered specie, the Irrawady dolphins (Orcealla Brevirostris). numbering 
55 are a unique natural heritage of Orissa, Chilka lake is one of the only two 
places in the world where these mammals are seen, the other being Songkhia 
lake in Thailand. 
Propellers of tourist boats kill or  seriously injure these dolphins 
whenever boats surround them. Curious t ourists always want to have a closer 
look at this rare mammal. With t he promotion of tour ism by the State 
Government, there has been a quantum jump in the number of tourists visiting 
Chilka, especially in winter. But, the tourism sans necessary precautions. It is 
becoming an encroachment on the rights of these animals. 
In view of their endangered status, these dolphins should receive the 
highest level of protection under law. It is true that tourism earns revenue for 
the country. But, at the same time, preserving our natural wealth and heritage 
should not be compromised with money, The Government should go in for 
projects like eco-tourism, which has been successfully experimented in Kerala.

[5 December, 2002] RAJYA SABHA  
Since dolphins are endangered and rare species of mammals, I 
appeal to the Government to presen/e these nature-friendly animals for th6 
posterity, by doing everything possible,  even if it amounts to losing some 
money by way of tourism.

Unreasonable tariff of telephone services 
SHRI CO, POULOSE (Kerala): Madam, my Special Menlion relates 
to telephone tariff, The Telecom Depart ment, while it was in charge of 
telephone operations, and now BSNL, has classified its operational areas as 
urban and rural.

the rural subscribers, The benefit of reduced rates is also available in respect 
of call charges, The BSNL has, arbitrarily, decided to bring almost all rural 
subscribers on a par with urban subscribers, and is overcharging them, 
The criterion for fixation of subscribers as rural/urban is the census 
figures. In States like Kerala, where t he population density is much high. the 
classification, according to the census data, is totally unrealistic, The ordinary 
telephone subscribers in villages are, mostly, ordinary/low-income people, and 
classifying them into the urban category will cause heavy hardships to them.

essential item for daily life. A large number of subscribers are finding it difficult 
to continue with the telephone connection with an increased tariff.

SHRI EDUAROO FALEIRO (Goa) : M adam, Deputy Chairman, over ' 
the last few decades, India had taken steps to become self-reliant in , armaments 
and established an R&D organisation and a Defence Industry to back it up. 
Indeed, unless we attain substantial ca pability for indigenous manufacture of

defence policies will remain hostage to nations and transnationals that supply us 
with the wherewithal of Defence. -Yet, Madam, steps taken during the last 50 
years towards self-reliance in Defence are now being seriously compromised. 
The Navy had prepared a 30-Year Submarine Building Plan which was intended 
to beat the "de facto" Submarine Technology Control Regime as well as revive 
building activities at the Mazagon Docks so that we become a genuine submarine 
building nation. The proposal was to build  20 submarines at an approximate cost 
of Rs. 15,000 crore over a period upto 2025. The Submarine building would be 
done in Mumbai and Vizag in a consortium with Indian firms like Larsen and 
Toubro, BHEL etc. with whom the Navy had detailed techno-commercial

finalised in 1997-98 by our Naval Submarine Design Bureau.

reported to cost the public excheque r a sum of Rs.12,500 crores for six 
SKD/CKD kits intended for assembly at Mazagon Docks, when the entiVe cost 
of the 20 submarines to be made under Project 75 India on both coasts was 
budgeted for Rs. 15,(300 crores, Govern ment must disclose the reasons for

Menace of ragging in the Country 
PROF, M. SANKARALINGAM (Tamil Nadu) : Madam, Deputy 
Chairman, the menace of ragging has raised its ugly head yet again in New 
Delhi: I am sure that this is not confined to any particular college in New Delhi. 
It is a regular and recurring feature in innumerable colleges all over the 
country, where freshers are humiliated and tortured by the seniors. These 
incidents invariably end up in tragic incidents like some freshers committing 
suicide and in a recent incident, two freshers going deaf. 
Recently, the Supreme Court of I ndia has warned that if educational 
institutions fail to curb ragging, its affili ations to the universities and financial 
aid could be withdrawn. The Government should set high standards to be 
followed by the seniors in treating freshe rs and should issue st rict instructions 
to be followed by the colleges / educationa l institutions to monitor the seniors 
as to whether they are indulging in ragging with a view to harassing the 
freshers, which results in unwanted heartburn and unwarranted hatred among 
seniors and juniors. 
It is high time, the Government should ban 'ragging' in colleges / 
educational institutions so that freshers are relieved of ragging by seniors in 
future. Here, I would like to  stress that the senior students of the Santosh 
Medical College, Ghaziabad, whose alleged ragging which has led to two 
freshers going deaf should not be al lowed to go scot-free. Many a time, 
incidents of ragging by seniors go unnoticed or do not come to light. Because 
the freshers take the ragging by seniors lying down, these types of incident 
continue till another incident catches the headlines in the newspapers. 
Therefore, I urge upon the Government to bring forward a stringent 
legislation and take all necessary steps to put an end to these activities. once 
for all.
